implementation_notes: serde_json::Value is the loosely typed, recursively composed document - Object(Map<String, Value>) with index/get/as_object for map-like access and Value::Array for children - and typed views are ordinary structs with #[derive(Deserialize)] reached through from_value or from_str, so the trait interfaces become a derive macro and a failed view becomes serde's error value instead of a cast exception. Where documents are built in memory rather than parsed, the manual realization is HashMap<String, Box<dyn Any>> with downcast_ref, the closest Rust has to a dynamic property bag.
pitfalls: from_value consumes the Value and fails as a whole: one bad field rejects the entire view, so keep the loose document by cloning it or by deserializing from &Value.
Indexing a Value returns Value::Null rather than erroring, so a typo produces a silent default; use get()/as_object() when absence must be distinguished from null.
A Box<dyn Any> bag requires 'static, so borrowed data cannot be stored, and downcast_ref returns None for a wrong type just as it does for a missing key.

variants.name: Box<dyn Any> property map with downcast views
variants.implementation_notes: The manual realization for documents that are built in code rather than parsed: the property map stores Box<dyn Any> and each view is an accessor whose getter calls downcast_ref::<T>(), which returns None when the stored type differs - the failure mode is an Option rather than a thrown cast error. Use it for extension state on long-lived objects where no serialisation format is involved; for anything that crosses a process or file boundary the serde_json variant is safer and cheaper to write.
pitfalls: downcast_ref returns None both for a missing key and for a wrong type, so the two failure modes collapse unless the accessor distinguishes them.
Box<dyn Any> erases auto traits: the map cannot cross threads or await points unless the trait object is Box<dyn Any + Send + Sync>.
